title: A Hybrid Retrieval Approach for Advancing Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
C02_notes: Proposes a hybrid text+KG retrieval pipeline to improve retriever accuracy in a health-tech RAG use case. While it briefly mentions 'false retrieval', it does not analyze, benchmark, or mitigate retrieval noise/robustness in a principled way, nor address adversarial attacks, conflicts, calibration, answerability, or distraction. It is a general RAG improvement method rather than a robust-RAG contribution.
C03_notes: General RAG application proposing a hybrid retriever combining text embeddings and knowledge-graph embeddings to improve retrieval accuracy in a health-tech use case. While it briefly motivates the work via 'false retrieval', the contribution is a retrieval-quality method, not a robustness, unreliable-evidence, adversarial, calibration, or answerability analysis. Out of scope for Map B.

title: Accelerating Inference of Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Sparse Context Selection
C02_notes: Efficiency-focused sparse context selection for RAG; mentions robustness as side benefit but primary focus is latency, not robust RAG evaluation.
C03_notes: Primary contribution is inference acceleration via sparse context selection (sparse KV-cache decoding), not robustness to unreliable evidence. The per-context assessment is in service of efficiency, though it incidentally filters irrelevant docs (touches noisy_retrieval and adaptive control). No threat model, no faithfulness/calibration evaluation, no robustness benchmark. Boundary context only.

title: AceSearcher: Bootstrapping Reasoning and Search for LLMs via Reinforced Self-Play
C02_notes: Generic multi-hop RAG capability paper using self-play RL for question decomposition and answer generation. Focuses on accuracy improvement on complex reasoning QA, not on robustness axes (noise, distraction, conflicts, attacks, calibration, answerability). No robust-RAG evaluation or mitigation.
C03_notes: Self-play RL training framework for multi-hop search-augmented LLMs via decomposer/solver roles. Focus is on improving reasoning and search effectiveness for complex QA, not on handling unreliable evidence, noisy retrieval, adversarial inputs, knowledge conflicts, or answerability. General RAG capability enhancement; closest taxonomy fit is calibration_control via adaptive decomposition-driven retrieval, but no robustness or evidence-quality analysis.

title: Attention in Large Language Models Yields Efficient Zero-Shot Re-Rankers
C02_notes: Proposes in-context re-ranking using LLM attention weights for efficient zero-shot re-ranking. Focuses on retrieval/re-ranking efficiency and accuracy, not on robustness of RAG to noise, adversarial perturbations, or context failures. Background relevance only.
C03_notes: Proposes in-context re-ranking (ICR) leveraging LLM attention weights for efficient zero-shot re-ranking. Focus is on efficiency and quality of re-ranking, not on robustness to unreliable evidence, adversarial corruption, knowledge conflicts, or selective prediction. Mentions calibration but only to mitigate attention biases (content-free query), not for abstention/control. Closest label is noisy_retrieval as better re-ranking reduces noisy context, but no explicit robustness contribution; treat as background/boundary.

title: BSharedRAG: Backbone Shared Retrieval-Augmented Generation for the E-commerce Domain
C02_notes: Domain-specific e-commerce RAG method paper proposing a shared backbone with LoRA modules for retriever and generator. Focus is on domain adaptation and parameter sharing, not on robustness, noise, distraction, conflict, adversarial, or calibration analysis. Out of scope for robust RAG map.
C03_notes: Domain-specific RAG framework for e-commerce using a shared LLM backbone with two LoRA modules for retrieval and generation. Contribution is architectural (parameter sharing, negative transfer avoidance, hard negative mining) and dataset construction (WorthBuying). Although the motivation mentions noisy/conflicting user-generated reviews and hallucinations, the paper does not analyze, evaluate, or mitigate retrieval noise, distraction, conflict, or adversarial conditions as a robustness contribution. General RAG method paper, not robust-RAG-under-unreliable-evidence.

title: Boosting the Potential of Large Language Models with an Intelligent Information Assistant
C02_notes: AssistRAG proposes an assistant LLM for memory and knowledge management to improve QA performance. While it includes a decision step on whether to use retrieved info, the focus is on boosting RAG capability rather than robustness, conflict, noise, or adversarial concerns. Background only.
C03_notes: AssistRAG is a general RAG enhancement framework with an intelligent assistant module for memory/knowledge management. While it includes plan-specification decisions ('Is Memory Useful?' / 'Is Knowledge Useful?') that touch on calibration/control, the primary contribution is improving complex reasoning QA performance via a trainable assistant plugin, not robustness under unreliable evidence. No explicit treatment of noisy retrieval, conflicts, attacks, or answerability. Borderline boundary context only.

title: C-3PO: Compact Plug-and-Play Proxy Optimization to Achieve Human-like Retrieval-Augmented Generation
C02_notes: C-3PO proposes a proxy-centric multi-agent framework with agents that decide when to retrieve, filter retrieved information, and determine sufficiency for answering. Addresses adaptive retrieval control and noisy retrieval filtering, relevant to robust RAG.
C03_notes: ICML 2025 proxy-centric multi-agent framework for RAG. Three agents handle: (1) Reasoning Router decides retrieval necessity and complexity (adaptive/selective retrieval), (2) Information Filter selects relevant docs (noise filtering), (3) Decision Maker assesses sufficiency to answer or continue retrieving. Core contribution is calibrated control over when/what to retrieve and what evidence to trust. Tested on OOD datasets including FreshQA and MultiHop-RAG. Borderline robust-RAG paper—primary focus is alignment/performance, but the adaptive retrieval gating and information filtering meaningfully address calibration_control and noisy_retrieval. Includes as support.

title: Can Knowledge-Graph-based Retrieval Augmented Generation Really Retrieve What You Need?
C02_notes: Proposes GraphFlow for accurate/diverse KG-based RAG retrieval on complex queries. Focus is on retrieval quality/diversity for KGs, not on robust RAG axes like noise, distractors, conflict, adversarial corruption, or calibration. Mentions robustness only as generalization to unseen KGs. Out of scope.
C03_notes: Proposes GraphFlow, a GFlowNet-style framework for KG-based RAG that retrieves accurate and diverse knowledge for complex queries via flow estimator + retrieval policy. Contribution is a general retrieval method improvement for complex multi-step KG queries (accuracy + diversity), not an analysis/mitigation of unreliable evidence, noise, conflict, adversarial corruption, or calibration. Mentions robustness/generalization to unseen KGs only briefly. Closest taxonomy match is noisy_retrieval as it concerns retrieval imperfection, but it does not explicitly evaluate/mitigate noise. Out of scope.

title: Chunk-Distilled Language Modeling
C02_notes: CD-LM is a retrieval-augmented language modeling method focused on inference efficiency (multi-token chunk generation) and training-free domain adaptation via chunk distillation. While it uses retrieval, it does not address robustness concerns such as noisy retrieval, distraction, knowledge conflict, adversarial attacks, uncertainty/calibration, or answerability. No robust RAG evaluation or mechanism. Out of scope.
C03_notes: CD-LM is a training-free chunk-level retrieval-augmented decoding method aimed at inference efficiency and knowledge adaptation (distillation/domain adaptation). It does not address unreliable evidence, noisy/adversarial retrieval, knowledge conflicts, calibration, abstention, or robustness evaluation. General RAG/efficiency contribution; out of scope for robust RAG map.

title: Context Tuning for Retrieval Augmented Generation
C02_notes: Paper proposes context tuning to improve tool retrieval and plan generation in RAG. Addresses underspecified queries but framed as retrieval enhancement for tool use, not robustness to noise/attacks/conflicts. Mentions hallucination reduction tangentially. Closest to ood_uncertainty (implicit queries) but lacks explicit robustness analysis or evaluation under adversarial/noisy conditions. Boundary background.
C03_notes: Paper proposes 'Context Tuning' to improve tool retrieval for underspecified/implicit queries in agentic RAG, using LambdaMART+RRF with usage signals. Although the venue is UncertaiNLP and the paper briefly mentions hallucination reduction, the core contribution is a retrieval-engineering method for tool selection, not analysis/mitigation of unreliable evidence, robustness perturbations, calibration, or adversarial conditions. Closest taxonomy fit is ood_uncertainty (implicit queries) but contribution is general RAG improvement, so excluded from map.

title: Cooperative Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Question Answering: Mutual Information Exchange and Ranking by Contrasting Layers
C02_notes: CoopRAG is a generic RAG framework improvement for multi-hop QA via query unrolling, contrasting-layer reranking, and reasoning chain completion. It does not explicitly study robustness to noise, distractors, conflicts, attacks, or uncertainty; evaluation is standard QA accuracy on HotpotQA/2Wiki/MuSiQue/NQ. No robust RAG angle.
C03_notes: CoopRAG proposes a cooperative RAG framework combining question unrolling (with uncertainty masking), unrolling-augmented retrieval, contrastive layer reranking, and reasoning chain completion for single/multi-hop QA. While it touches on incorrect retrievals and LLM uncertainty, the main contribution is a general RAG architecture aimed at improving retrieval and QA accuracy rather than a focused study of unreliable evidence, adversarial robustness, calibration, or evaluation of robustness. Boundary case; primary lab noisy_retrieval as closest fit.

title: Crafting Personalized Agents through Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Editable Memory Graphs
C02_notes: Application paper on personalized agents using editable memory graphs with RL-based adaptive memory selection. Mentions noise from irrelevant memories and adaptive selection but does not systematically study RAG robustness, attacks, or evaluation. Out of scope for robust RAG map.
C03_notes: EMG-RAG is a personalized RAG application using editable memory graphs and RL-based adaptive memory selection for smartphone AI assistants. While it uses adaptive selection (loose connection to calibration_control) and briefly mentions noise from irrelevant memories, the core contribution is personalization, memory management, and end-to-end optimization, not robustness under unreliable evidence, adversarial attacks, knowledge conflicts, or answerability. Out of scope for robust RAG map.

title: DSLR: Document Refinement with Sentence-Level Re-ranking and Reconstruction to Enhance Retrieval-Augmented Generation
C02_notes: DSLR proposes unsupervised sentence-level re-ranking and reconstruction to filter irrelevant/redundant info from retrieved passages, directly addressing noisy retrieval and LLM distraction in RAG. Workshop paper at ACL KnowledgeNLP 2024, evaluated on open-domain QA benchmarks. Fits robust RAG context-refinement mitigation.
C03_notes: DSLR decomposes retrieved passages into sentences, re-ranks them, and reconstructs coherent passages to filter out irrelevant/redundant info that distracts LLMs. Explicit mitigation for retrieval noise and distractor content in RAG context. Workshop paper at KnowledgeNLP@ACL 2024.

title: EAReranker: Efficient Embedding Adequacy Assessment for Retrieval Augmented Generation
C02_notes: Embedding-based reranker focused on efficiency/privacy and adequacy scoring; only tangentially touches filtering inadequate documents, lacks explicit robustness evaluation.
C03_notes: Efficient embedding-based reranker that scores document 'adequacy' (verifiability, coverage, completeness, structure) instead of pure relevance, claiming to filter inadequate docs that could mislead RAG. However, the paper's primary contributions are computational efficiency (constant memory, 2-3x faster) and privacy (no plaintext access), not analysis/mitigation of unreliable evidence, distractors, conflicts, or adversarial corruption. Borderline case; closest taxonomy fit is noisy_retrieval since it filters low-utility docs, but framing is general reranking improvement rather than a robustness-under-unreliable-evidence contribution.

title: Entity-Focused Dense Passage Retrieval for Outside-Knowledge Visual Question Answering
C02_notes: Paper proposes Entity-Focused Dense Passage Retrieval for OK-VQA. It improves retrieval quality for multimodal QA but does not study robustness of RAG against noise, distractors, conflicts, adversarial attacks, or calibration. Out of scope for the robust RAG map.
C03_notes: Multimodal RAG retrieval improvement for OK-VQA via entity-focused dense passage retrieval. Although the paper notes retrieved knowledge is often inadequate/too general (weak supervision), the contribution is a better retriever for VQA, not robustness analysis, mitigation of unreliable evidence, calibration, conflict handling, or adversarial defense. Out of scope for robust RAG under unreliable evidence.

title: FiD-Light: Efficient and Effective Retrieval-Augmented Text Generation
C02_notes: FiD-Light focuses on efficiency-effectiveness tradeoffs in retrieval-augmented generation, not on robustness aspects such as noisy retrieval, adversarial attack, knowledge conflict, or calibration. While it touches on robustness of source pointing distribution shift, this is a minor architectural choice rather than a robust RAG study. Background/foundational RAG work, not core evidence for the robust RAG map.
C03_notes: FiD-Light focuses on efficiency-effectiveness tradeoff in retrieval-augmented generation via compressing encoder-decoder information flow and adding source-pointer re-ranking. Evaluated on KILT for combined text generation + provenance precision. While it briefly discusses robustness of source pointers to distribution shifts in #relevant passages, the main contribution is efficiency, not unreliable evidence, conflict, adversarial, or calibration. Background only.

title: Graph-KV: Breaking Sequence via Injecting Structural Biases into Large Language Models
C02_notes: Graph-KV addresses positional bias and serialization issues in RAG by structuring KV-cache attention via source-target relationships. Evaluated on 7 RAG benchmarks including multi-hop reasoning and long-document understanding. Directly tackles context utilization robustness.
C03_notes: Graph-KV is primarily an architectural/efficiency contribution that modifies KV-cache attention to inject structural inductive biases for RAG and graph-structured data. It reduces positional bias and supports parallel encoding of retrieved chunks, with evaluation on RAG/multi-hop benchmarks. While it touches positional bias and notes noisy multi-hop reasoning, the central contribution is structural encoding/efficiency rather than analyzing or mitigating unreliable evidence (no retrieval noise, conflict, attack, abstention, or answerability analysis). Closest taxonomy fit is distraction (positional bias/context utilization), but out of map scope.

title: Hierarchical Planning for Complex Tasks with Knowledge Graph-RAG and Symbolic Verification
C02_notes: Paper proposes a neuro-symbolic hierarchical planning method (HVR) that integrates KG-based RAG and symbolic verification for robotic task planning. RAG is used as a knowledge source for planning, but the paper does not study retrieval robustness, noisy/adversarial retrieval, knowledge conflict, calibration, or evaluate RAG robustness specifically. Robustness here refers to plan correctness via symbolic validation, not RAG robustness. Out of scope for robust RAG map.
C03_notes: Paper integrates KG-based RAG with hierarchical planning and a symbolic validator for robotic task planning. RAG is a knowledge source component, not the subject of robustness analysis. Symbolic verifier addresses plan correctness/failure detection (an agentic control mechanism) rather than unreliable retrieval evidence (noise, conflict, attack, ambiguity). Primary contribution is neuro-symbolic agentic planning; closest taxonomy fit is multimodal_agentic_code but the paper is not centered on RAG robustness under unreliable evidence.

title: Holistic Reasoning with Long-Context LMs: A Benchmark for Database Operations on Massive Textual Data
C02_notes: HoloBench benchmarks long-context LMs vs RAG on holistic reasoning over large textual data, varying context length, info density, position, and query complexity. Relevant to RAG evaluation and long-context distraction analysis, though framed as LCLM benchmark contrasted with RAG.
C03_notes: HoloBench is a long-context LM benchmark testing holistic/aggregation reasoning by mixing relevant and irrelevant verbalized DB rows; it discusses RAG limitations and controls information density/position (distraction-adjacent). However, the main contribution is evaluating LCLM capabilities, not robustness of RAG under unreliable evidence. Boundary/background context only.

title: HyPA-RAG: A Hybrid Parameter Adaptive Retrieval-Augmented Generation System for AI Legal and Policy Applications
C02_notes: Domain RAG system with adaptive parameter selection, hybrid retrieval, and custom evaluation framework targeting common RAG failure points in legal/policy QA.
C03_notes: Domain-specific legal/policy RAG system (NYC LL144) featuring a query complexity classifier for adaptive parameter tuning, hybrid (dense/sparse/KG) retrieval, and a custom RAGAS-style evaluation framework. While it mentions common RAG failure points and includes some adaptive-control flavor, the contribution is primarily an application-oriented system with domain evaluation, not a robustness-to-unreliable-evidence study. Closest taxonomy hook is calibration_control (query-conditioned parameter adaptation), with secondary evaluation_benchmark for the custom question types and metrics.

title: Improving Retrieval-Augmented Generation through Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
C02_notes: Paper proposes MMOA-RAG, a multi-agent RL framework to jointly optimize query rewriter, retriever, selector, and generator modules in a RAG pipeline. Focus is on end-to-end optimization for answer F1, not on robustness aspects (noise, distraction, conflict, adversarial, calibration). No explicit robust RAG angle, so out of scope.
C03_notes: MMOA-RAG proposes multi-agent RL to jointly optimize a standard RAG pipeline (query rewriter, retriever, selector, generator) toward F1 reward. Although the selector module filters documents and the system arguably learns to use evidence, the paper's contribution is general end-to-end pipeline optimization, not robustness to unreliable evidence, noise, conflict, adversarial corruption, or calibrated abstention. No explicit perturbation/noise/attack evaluation. Out of scope; closest taxonomy bucket is calibration_control via the selector + joint reward decisioning.

title: KnowGPT: Knowledge Graph based Prompting for Large Language Models
C02_notes: KnowGPT is a KG-based prompting framework using RL and MAB for knowledge extraction and prompt construction. Focus is on effectiveness and cost of GraphRAG for QA, not on robustness analysis (no explicit study of noise, conflicts, adversarial corruption, or calibration). Background/boundary for robust RAG map.
C03_notes: General GraphRAG/KG-prompting framework using deep RL for knowledge extraction and MAB for prompt construction. Main contributions target three issues: huge search space, high API cost, and laborious prompt design. While it briefly mentions data quality issues in motivation, the actual work is a standard KG-RAG QA method focused on efficiency and accuracy, not robustness to unreliable evidence, adversarial attacks, conflicts, or calibration. Out of scope.

title: Knowledge-Consistent Dialogue Generation with Knowledge Graphs
C02_notes: SURGE proposes subgraph retrieval-augmented dialogue generation with KG, addressing irrelevant knowledge and hallucination via contrastive learning. While related to faithfulness and noisy retrieval, focus is on KG-grounded dialogue generation rather than robust RAG evaluation or attack/defense. Background relevance only.
C03_notes: KG-augmented dialogue generation (SURGE). Explicitly analyzes irrelevant retrieval (87% of 1-hop KG facts irrelevant) and proposes context-relevant subgraph retrieval plus graph-text contrastive learning to enforce faithfulness/consistency with retrieved knowledge. Addresses unreliable evidence (noisy KG facts) and hallucination, but in dialogue/KG setting rather than open-domain text RAG—hence support, not core.

title: Knowledge-Consistent Dialogue Generation with Language Models and Knowledge Graphs
C02_notes: SURGE is a KG-augmented dialogue generation method that retrieves relevant subgraphs and uses contrastive learning to enforce knowledge consistency. While it touches on filtering irrelevant facts and reducing hallucination, it predates the LLM-RAG robustness literature and does not explicitly study robust RAG attacks, defenses, or systematic robustness evaluation. Background only.
C03_notes: SURGE: KG-augmented dialogue generation that explicitly tackles irrelevant retrieval (87% of 1-hop facts are irrelevant) via GNN-based subgraph retrieval and addresses hallucination/faithfulness via graph-text contrastive learning. Introduces KQA metric for faithfulness evaluation. Borderline support: not framed as adversarial robustness, but addresses noisy retrieval and knowledge consistency as core contributions.

title: LI-RAGE: Late Interaction Retrieval Augmented Generation with Explicit Signals for Open-Domain Table Question Answering
C02_notes: Paper proposes LI-RAGE for open-domain TableQA with late interaction retrieval and binary relevance token. Focus is on improving SOTA accuracy, not robustness to noise, attacks, or conflicts. Not a robust RAG contribution.
C03_notes: Open-domain TableQA method paper combining ColBERT late interaction retrieval, RAGE joint training, and a binary yes/no relevance token prefix to filter non-gold retrieved tables. The relevance-token mechanism has a tangential connection to deciding when retrieved evidence is reliable, but the paper's primary contribution is SOTA on NQ-TABLES and E2E-WTQ, not robustness under unreliable evidence, knowledge conflict, adversarial corruption, or systematic evaluation of noisy retrieval. General RAG application; exclude from map.

title: LLM-Check: Investigating Detection of Hallucinations in Large Language Models
C02_notes: LLM-Check proposes hallucination detection using internal attention/hidden states/probabilities; explicitly includes RAG setting with RAGTruth dataset. Relevant to robust RAG via hallucination/faithfulness detection, though RAG is only one of several evaluation settings.
C03_notes: Proposes LLM-Check, a hallucination detection method using internal attention maps, hidden states, and output probabilities of an auxiliary LLM. Includes evaluation on RAGTruth (RAG-specific hallucination benchmark) where ground-truth references are available, making it relevant to detecting unreliable/ungrounded generation in RAG. Primary contribution is detection enabling trust decisions, hence calibration_control; secondary knowledge_conflict because RAG hallucinations often reflect conflict between parametric and retrieved evidence. Not a core RAG robustness paper but a useful supporting tool.

title: LLMs as Collaborator: Demands-Guided Collaborative Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Commonsense Knowledge-Grounded Open-Domain Dialogue Systems
C02_notes: Generic RAG method paper for commonsense knowledge-grounded open-domain dialogue. Proposes DCRAG using LLMs as collaborators to retrieve from knowledge graphs. No explicit robustness angle: no analysis of retrieval noise, no adversarial attacks, no knowledge conflicts, no calibration/abstention. Out of scope for robust RAG map.
C03_notes: Method paper proposing collaborative RAG (DCRAG) for commonsense knowledge-grounded dialogue. Focus is on better identifying retrieval demands via LLM-retriever collaboration to improve response quality. Mentions hallucination/outdated knowledge as motivation, but contribution is a general RAG improvement for dialogue, not a robustness/unreliable-evidence/security/calibration/conflict mechanism. Out of scope.

title: Lift Yourself Up: Retrieval-augmented Text Generation with Self-Memory
C02_notes: Generic RAG improvement method using self-generated memory iteratively. Focuses on text generation quality (MT, summarization, dialogue) without any robustness angle - no analysis of noisy retrieval, distraction, conflicts, attacks, calibration, or answerability. Out of scope for robust RAG map.
C03_notes: Selfmem proposes using model's own output as iterative self-memory to overcome fixed-corpus quality limitations in retrieval-augmented generation (MT, summarization, dialogue). Focuses on generation quality improvement via memory selection, not on robustness against unreliable evidence, adversarial corruption, knowledge conflicts, calibration, or answerability. General RAG quality-enhancement method — out of scope for robust RAG under unreliable evidence.

title: M-RAG: Reinforcing Large Language Model Performance through Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Multiple Partitions
C02_notes: M-RAG proposes a multi-partition RAG framework with multi-agent RL to improve generation quality on summarization, translation, and dialogue tasks. While it briefly mentions noise from coarse-grained retrieval, the paper focuses on performance improvement rather than robustness analysis, attack/defense, calibration, or evaluation of robust RAG axes. Not a robust RAG contribution.
C03_notes: M-RAG proposes a multi-partition paradigm with multi-agent RL (Agent-S for partition selection, Agent-R for memory refinement) to improve RAG performance on summarization, translation, and dialogue generation. While motivation briefly mentions noise from coarse-grained AKNN retrieval, the contribution is a general performance-improvement method, not a robustness/unreliable-evidence study. No adversarial, conflict, calibration, or evaluation-of-robustness contribution. Out of scope.

title: Modeling Uncertainty and Using Post-fusion as Fallback Improves Retrieval Augmented Generation with LLMs
C02_notes: Paper investigates uncertainty modeling (LLM 'unknown' outputs) and proposes post-fusion fallback and concatenation-as-distiller strategies to improve RAG when retrieved passages contain the answer but the model fails. Addresses calibration/control (when to fall back) and distraction from retrieved passages. Tested on NQ, TriviaQA, SQuAD. Directly relevant to robust RAG.
C03_notes: Paper models LLM uncertainty via 'unknown' outputs and proposes post-fusion as fallback strategy when concatenation fails. Addresses calibration/fallback decisions (when to switch strategy) and distraction (LLM fails even when correct passage is in top-k under oracle setting). Multi-round feedback approaches. Workshop paper at KnowLLM 2024, useful support for robust RAG positioning.

title: Multi-Hop Paragraph Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
C02_notes: Paper proposes MUPPET, an iterative multi-hop paragraph retrieval method for open-domain QA (SQuAD-Open, HotpotQA). It is a retrieval/QA architecture contribution, not a study of robustness, noise, distraction, conflict, adversarial perturbation, calibration, or answerability. While multi-hop retrieval is foundational background for downstream RAG robustness work, it does not explicitly analyze, benchmark, attack, or mitigate retrieval/context robustness. Out of scope for robust RAG map.
C03_notes: MUPPET proposes an iterative multi-hop paragraph retrieval method for open-domain QA (SQuAD-Open, HotpotQA). It is a general retrieval/QA methodology paper without explicit analysis or mitigation of unreliable evidence, robustness, adversarial threats, calibration, or evidence quality. Out of scope; closest taxonomy bucket is noisy_retrieval only by virtue of being a retrieval method.

title: Multi-Level Information Retrieval Augmented Generation for Knowledge-based Visual Question Answering
C02_notes: Multi-level entity+passage RAG for KB-VQA. Mentions noisy pseudo-relevance and irrelevant passage issues, but focus is on improving accuracy via multi-level retrieval, not robustness analysis or defenses. Boundary multimodal RAG work.
C03_notes: Multimodal RAG method (MiRAG) for Knowledge-based VQA that introduces multi-level retrieval (entity + passage) with query expansion and end-to-end joint training. While the motivation briefly mentions noisy/pseudo-relevant retrieval signals, the main contribution is improving retrieval quality and answer accuracy on ViQuAE benchmark, not robustness under unreliable evidence, attacks, conflicts, calibration, or answerability. Standard multimodal RAG application; out of scope for robust RAG map.

title: Multi-Task Dense Retrieval via Model Uncertainty Fusion for Open-Domain Question Answering
C02_notes: Paper proposes multi-task dense retrieval via ensemble model uncertainty fusion across DPR experts for open-domain QA. Uncertainty estimation is used as a dynamic weighting scheme for expert selection, not for RAG calibration, abstention, or robustness against noisy/adversarial/conflicting retrieval. No RAG generator-side analysis, no robustness threat model. Generic dense retrieval contribution; out of scope for robust RAG map.
C03_notes: Multi-task DPR that uses ensemble model uncertainty (mutual information) to weight predictions from different domain-specific retrievers. 'Corpus inconsistency' here refers to training data overlap across QA datasets, not contradictions among retrieved evidence. Uncertainty is used for expert selection rather than for assessing evidence quality, abstention, or robustness against unreliable evidence. Closest taxonomy label is calibration_control because of the uncertainty-weighted fusion, but the contribution is about multi-task retrieval optimization, not robust RAG under unreliable evidence.

title: Neural Graph Matching Improves Retrieval Augmented Generation in Molecular Machine Learning
C02_notes: Domain-specific RAG for molecular machine learning (mass spectrum simulation) using neural graph matching. While it mentions noise-robust matching, robustness pertains to structural ambiguity in retrieved molecules for GNNs, not LLM-based RAG robustness. Not about retrieval noise, distraction, conflicts, attacks, or calibration in LLM RAG.
C03_notes: Domain-specific RAG application for molecular mass spectrum simulation using neural graph matching. While it mentions noise-robust matching, this refers to robustness in graph affinity learning for molecular structures, not robustness of RAG under unreliable evidence. No contribution on retrieval noise analysis, conflicts, adversarial attacks, calibration, or robust RAG evaluation. Out of scope.

title: NutriBench: A Dataset for Evaluating Large Language Models in Nutrition Estimation from Meal Descriptions
C02_notes: Domain-specific (nutrition) benchmark that evaluates LLMs with standard, CoT, and RAG prompting on carbohydrate estimation. RAG is used only as one prompting strategy; no robustness analysis (no noise, distraction, conflict, adversarial, calibration, or answerability angle) for RAG. Out of scope for the robust RAG map.
C03_notes: Domain-specific (nutrition) benchmark for evaluating LLMs on carbohydrate estimation from meal descriptions. RAG is tested as one of several prompting strategies but the paper does not address unreliable evidence, retrieval robustness, conflicts, attacks, calibration, or any robust-RAG axis. Out of scope; closest taxonomy is multimodal_agentic_code (domain-specific RAG setting) with evaluation_benchmark as secondary.

title: Online Adaptation of Language Models with a Memory of Amortized Contexts
C02_notes: Paper proposes Memory of Amortized Contexts (MAC), an online adaptation framework for LLMs using PEFT modulations and amortization-based meta-learning. While it briefly mentions RAG as a complementary method and notes counterfactual sensitivity, the core contribution is about efficient online finetuning/adaptation, not robust RAG mechanisms. No explicit analysis of retrieval noise, distraction, conflict, or adversarial robustness.
C03_notes: MAC proposes an online adaptation framework using amortized context modulations stored in a memory bank to update a frozen LM efficiently. The main contributions are computational/memory efficiency and knowledge retention, not robustness to unreliable evidence. Although the paper briefly notes that retrieved documents may contain counterfactual information and shows MAC can complement RAG (e.g., improving over BM25), it does not analyze, mitigate, or evaluate noisy/adversarial/conflicting evidence in a robust-RAG sense. Treated as background/boundary.

title: Optimizing Retrieval for RAG via Reinforcement Learning
C02_notes: Paper proposes R3, an RL-based retrieval optimization framework for RAG. While it mentions retrieval gaps (semantically related but unhelpful content, misleading evidence), the focus is on improving RAG retrieval performance via RL rather than robustness to noise, adversarial attacks, or conflicts. Not directly a robust RAG paper; closest category is noisy retrieval as background.
C03_notes: R3 is a retriever optimization framework using RL with downstream RAG rewards. While it acknowledges the IR-RAG gap (retrievers returning semantically related but unhelpful or misleading content), the core contribution is a training paradigm (reinforced contrastive learning) for better retrieval, not an analysis/mitigation of unreliable evidence, robustness, calibration, or security. General RAG improvement work, marginal to the map.

title: Patent Response System Optimised for Faithfulness: Procedural Knowledge Embodiment with Knowledge Graph and Retrieval Augmented Generation
C02_notes: Domain-specific patent response system using RAG and KG. Focuses on faithfulness in patent domain, not on robust RAG mechanisms broadly applicable. No analysis of retrieval noise, conflicts, attacks, or calibration. Out of scope.
C03_notes: Domain-specific RAG+KG system for patent Office Action responses. Although it reports faithfulness improvement across six error types, the contribution is a procedural-knowledge integration pipeline (PPNet KG + PRLLM + RAG) for a patent application, not an analysis or mitigation of unreliable evidence, retrieval noise, conflict, or adversarial corruption. Boundary at most.

title: PlanRAG: A Plan-then-Retrieval Augmented Generation for Generative Large Language Models as Decision Makers
C02_notes: PlanRAG proposes an iterative plan-then-retrieve RAG technique for decision-making QA over structured databases with a new DQA benchmark. Focus is on planning capability for complex decisions, not on robustness against noise, distraction, conflict, attacks, or calibration. Not a robust RAG contribution.
C03_notes: PlanRAG proposes iterative plan-then-retrieve RAG for a new Decision QA task on graph/relational DBs, with a DQA benchmark from video games. The contribution is a task-decomposition/planning method and decision-making benchmark, not a study of unreliable evidence (noise, conflicts, attacks, distractors, uncertainty, abstention, calibration). The iterative re-planning loosely resembles adaptive retrieval (calibration_control) but is not framed as a robustness mechanism. Out of scope for robust RAG under unreliable evidence.

title: Quebec Automobile Insurance Question-Answering With Retrieval-Augmented Generation
C02_notes: Domain-specific application of RAG for Quebec automobile insurance QA. Introduces corpora and evaluates GPT-4o, but does not focus on robustness, noise, attacks, calibration, or systematic robust RAG analysis. Background/application paper without robust RAG angle.
C03_notes: Domain-specific (Quebec automobile insurance) RAG application paper. Creates two French corpora and evaluates GPT-4o with RAG, reporting 5-13% factually incorrect answers. While it discusses hallucination/reliability concerns in a critical domain, the contribution is primarily a domain corpus and evaluation, not a generalizable robust RAG method or analysis of unreliable evidence. Falls outside core robust-RAG scope but touches on faithfulness/reliability as boundary context.

title: R$^2$AG: Incorporating Retrieval Information into Retrieval Augmented Generation
C02_notes: R2AG bridges the semantic gap between retrievers and LLMs via a R2-Former and retrieval-aware prompting. Explicitly addresses noisy/low-quality retrieved documents and lost-in-middle issues; claims robustness in experiments. Primary angle is mitigation of retrieval noise via context assembly, with distraction as secondary. EMNLP Findings 2024.
C03_notes: R2AG proposes an architectural enhancement (R2-Former) to bridge semantic gap between retriever and LLM via retrieval-aware prompting. While the paper mentions low-quality documents and validates 'robustness' as one of its claimed properties, the primary contribution is a general RAG framework improvement rather than a method specifically targeting unreliable evidence, noise handling, or evidence quality control. Closest taxonomy fit is noisy_retrieval as a secondary motivation, but core contribution is not robust RAG under unreliable evidence.

title: RAG-HAT: A Hallucination-Aware Tuning Pipeline for LLM in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
C02_notes: RAG-HAT proposes hallucination-aware fine-tuning pipeline with detection and DPO-based mitigation for RAG outputs, directly addressing faithfulness/context-grounding robustness in RAG.
C03_notes: RAG-HAT proposes a hallucination-aware tuning pipeline: trains a detection model to identify span-level hallucinations and provide explanations, then uses GPT-4 Turbo to rewrite outputs and applies DPO to fine-tune the generator for improved contextual faithfulness. Maps to knowledge_conflict (contextual faithfulness to retrieved evidence) with mitigation at the generator. Evaluated on RAGTruth. Not a benchmark contribution itself, but a solid mitigation method for hallucination/unfaithful generation in RAG.

title: RAG-SR: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Neural Symbolic Regression
C02_notes: Applies a retrieval-augmented generation mechanism to neural symbolic regression to reduce hallucinations in generated symbolic trees. Not about robustness of RAG for LLM QA/text retrieval; uses RAG only as a domain technique in symbolic regression.
C03_notes: Domain-specific application of RAG to neural symbolic regression. Uses retrieval to ground LM-generated symbolic trees and reduce hallucination, but contribution is a new SR method, not a study/evaluation/defense of RAG robustness under unreliable evidence. Out of scope for robust RAG map.

title: RAG-Studio: Towards In-Domain Adaptation of Retrieval Augmented Generation Through Self-Alignment
C02_notes: Self-aligned domain adaptation framework jointly fine-tuning retriever and generator; touches noisy context handling via helpful/irrelevant/misleading classification but primary focus is domain adaptation, not robustness.
C03_notes: Primary contribution is in-domain adaptation of RAG via self-aligned synthetic data and joint fine-tuning of retriever+generator. While the framework does train the LLM with CoT rationale to classify context as helpful/irrelevant/misleading and to withstand noisy contexts (citing Yoran et al., RAFT), this noise-robustness is auxiliary to the main domain-adaptation goal. Not a focused unreliable-evidence/robustness contribution; out of map B core scope but tangential to noisy_retrieval.

title: RAG4GFM: Bridging Knowledge Gaps in Graph Foundation Models through Graph Retrieval Augmented Generation
C02_notes: Paper proposes RAG4GFM, a graph-RAG framework for Graph Foundation Models with multi-level graph indexing, task-aware retrieval, and graph fusion. Focus is knowledge updating and reasoning fidelity for GFMs, not robust RAG concerns. No analysis of retrieval noise, distractors, conflicts, attacks, or abstention. Out of scope.
C03_notes: General graph-RAG framework for Graph Foundation Models proposing multi-level indexing, task-aware retrieval, and graph fusion to improve knowledge updating efficiency and reduce hallucinations. While 'faithful reasoning' is mentioned as motivation, the paper does not analyze unreliable evidence, noisy/adversarial retrieval, knowledge conflict, calibration, or robustness benchmarks; it is a standard graph-RAG method paper. Closest taxonomy bucket is multimodal_agentic_code (graph-specific RAG), but out of scope for robust-RAG-under-unreliable-evidence map.

title: RAGLAB: A Modular and Research-Oriented Unified Framework for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
C02_notes: RAGLAB is a generic modular RAG framework for fair comparison of 6 RAG algorithms across 10 benchmarks. It is a general-purpose research toolkit/library without specific focus on robustness, adversarial settings, noise, distractors, or knowledge conflicts. Useful as background/positioning for RAG evaluation infrastructure but not direct evidence for robust RAG.
C03_notes: RAGLAB is a modular open-source framework for reproducing and fairly comparing 6 RAG algorithms across 10 benchmarks. It is general RAG infrastructure/tooling without a specific contribution to unreliable evidence, robustness, adversarial threat, calibration, or answerability. Closest taxonomy label is evaluation_benchmark due to its fair-comparison and evaluation focus, but it does not target robustness axes.

title: RAGRouter: Learning to Route Queries to Multiple Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
C02_notes: RAGRouter learns to route queries across multiple retrieval-augmented LLMs based on their differing RAG capabilities. While it touches on heterogeneous robustness to retrieval noise, the core contribution is model selection/routing rather than robustness analysis, mitigation, or evaluation of retrieval failures. Out of scope for robust RAG map.
C03_notes: Proposes RAGRouter, a contrastive-learning router that selects the best LLM from a pool for each RAG query, modeling document/RAG-capability embeddings. Primary contribution is multi-model routing for performance/efficiency, not handling unreliable evidence. Only a small appendix section (G) touches noisy retrieval. Closest taxonomy fit is calibration_control (system-level model selection decision); secondary noisy_retrieval for the appendix analysis. Out of scope for robust RAG under unreliable evidence.

title: RAGViz: Diagnose and Visualize Retrieval-Augmented Generation
C02_notes: RAGViz visualizes attention on retrieved docs to diagnose hallucinations from parametric vs retrieved sources, supporting context utilization analysis.
C03_notes: EMNLP system demonstration paper presenting RAGViz, a visualization/diagnostic tool that displays token- and document-level attention from LLM generation to retrieved passages, with document toggling for side-by-side comparison. It can help users qualitatively distinguish hallucinations stemming from parametric memory vs retrieved (external) memory, which loosely touches on knowledge conflict and document utility. However, the paper does not propose a robustness method, defense, benchmark, calibration mechanism, or quantitative evaluation of unreliable evidence; it is primarily a tool/utility. Treated as background context only.

title: RAPID: Long-Context Inference with Retrieval-Augmented Speculative Decoding
C02_notes: RAPID is an inference acceleration method combining RAG with speculative decoding for long-context LLMs. Focus is efficiency/throughput, not robustness. Brief robustness-to-retrieval-quality analysis is incidental, not a robust RAG contribution.
C03_notes: RAPID is a long-context inference acceleration method using RAG as a drafter for speculative decoding. The primary contribution is efficiency (throughput speedup) and quality enhancement via knowledge transfer from RAG drafter to long-context target LLM. While the paper briefly mentions 'robustness to retrieval quality' as a side analysis, the work is not about unreliable evidence, noisy retrieval mitigation, calibration, security, or answerability. It is a decoding/efficiency method rather than a robust-RAG contribution, so out of scope.

title: ReFIR: Grounding Large Restoration Models with Retrieval Augmentation
C02_notes: Image restoration with retrieved reference images; uses RAG analogy but applied to vision, not LLM RAG robustness. Out of scope.
C03_notes: Applies retrieval augmentation concept to image restoration (LRMs) using retrieved HQ reference images to mitigate visual hallucination. This is a multimodal generative application, not a study of unreliable evidence, robustness, attacks, calibration, or evaluation of robust RAG. Out of scope for Map B.

title: ReMindRAG: Low-Cost LLM-Guided Knowledge Graph Traversal for Efficient RAG
C02_notes: Proposes KG-RAG system with LLM-guided graph traversal and memory replay for cost-effective multi-hop retrieval. Focus is on effectiveness/efficiency trade-off, not robustness to noise, attacks, conflicts, or uncertainty. No explicit robust RAG angle.
C03_notes: KG-RAG system focused on cost efficiency and effectiveness via LLM-guided graph traversal with memory replay. No specific contribution to robustness under unreliable evidence, adversarial threats, calibration, or answerability. Brief mention of reducing 'irrelevant noise' is incidental to the efficiency goal. General RAG method, out of scope.

title: RealRAG: Retrieval-augmented Realistic Image Generation via Self-reflective Contrastive Learning
C02_notes: RealRAG is a retrieval-augmented framework for text-to-image generation that uses a reflective retriever to improve realism for fine-grained/novel object generation. While it is multimodal RAG, the focus is on generation quality and bridging knowledge gaps in image generators, not on robustness aspects like noisy retrieval analysis, adversarial corruption, knowledge conflicts, or calibration. It does not study or evaluate robustness of RAG in any of the taxonomy senses, so it is out of scope for
C03_notes: RealRAG is a retrieval-augmented framework for text-to-image generation using self-reflective contrastive learning to retrieve images that compensate for missing knowledge in generative models. Focus is on improving image realism/FID, not on robustness under unreliable evidence, adversarial corruption, conflict resolution, calibration, or answerability. General multimodal RAG application without an unreliable-evidence/robustness contribution.

title: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding
C02_notes: Paper proposes new training objectives (DKS, RAC) to improve retriever generalization in RAG by addressing false-negative passage problem. Robustness mentioned is about training generalization, not handling noisy/adversarial context or evaluating robustness axes. Not core robust RAG.
C03_notes: Paper proposes new RAG training objectives (DKS and RAC) using rich answer encoding to capture knowledge-relevant (not just label-relevant) passages on MSMARCO and KILT-WoW. While the word 'robust' appears, the contribution is a general retrieval/training improvement for KIG, not an analysis or mitigation of unreliable evidence, distraction, conflict, adversarial corruption, calibration, or evaluation of robustness. Closest taxonomy bucket is noisy_retrieval (false-negative passage problem in training data), but it is out of scope for robust RAG under unreliable evidence.

title: Retrieval augmented text-to-SQL generation for epidemiological question answering using electronic health records
C02_notes: Domain-specific RAG application for text-to-SQL on EHR/claims data. Uses RAG to improve SQL generation but does not study robustness, noise, distraction, conflicts, attacks, or calibration. No robust RAG angle.
C03_notes: Domain-specific RAG application for text-to-SQL on EHR/claims data for epidemiological QA. Demonstrates that retrieving similar Q-SQL pairs improves accuracy over static prompting, but provides no contribution on unreliable evidence, robustness, conflict, adversarial attacks, calibration, or answerability. Standard RAG efficacy study in a clinical setting — out of scope for robust RAG under unreliable evidence.

title: Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge
C02_notes: Thesis proposal at NAACL SRW surveying RAG and proposing extensions to heterogeneous knowledge sources (text, tables, KGs). Briefly notes that scaling to CCNet hurts NQ/HotpotQA performance, but the focus is improving coverage/knowledge integration, not robustness, noise mitigation, conflict handling, calibration, or attacks. Background only; not direct evidence for the robust RAG map.
C03_notes: NAACL SRW thesis proposal on RAG across heterogeneous knowledge sources (text/tables/KGs) to improve coverage. Briefly notes that scaling to CCNet hurts performance due to lower-quality web content, but the paper's contribution is knowledge integration, not analyzing/mitigating unreliable evidence, distraction, conflict, or adversarial corruption. Out of scope for robust RAG.

title: Retrieval-augmented generation in multilingual settings
C02_notes: Studies mRAG pipeline across 13 languages, evaluating retrieval and generation robustness in multilingual settings; identifies limitations like irrelevant retrieval, code-switching, and metric adjustments. Relevant as evaluation/benchmarking work for RAG robustness in cross-lingual setting.
C03_notes: Paper establishes a multilingual RAG (mRAG) baseline across 13 languages, studying retriever/generator/evaluation components. Primary contribution is a baseline pipeline and analysis of multilingual settings, not a robustness mechanism for unreliable evidence. While it mentions limitations like wrong document reading and irrelevant retrieval, and notes evaluation metric needs adjustment for multilingual settings, these are not the central contributions. Closest taxonomy fit is multimodal_agentic_code (domain-specific RAG setting), but lacks unique robustness mechanism. Useful as background for multilingual RAG context.

title: Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling
C02_notes: Paper uses robust in title but the robustness refers mainly to domain adaptation (zero/few-shot transfer to new TACRED variant) and hard negative mining for DPR in slot filling, not to noise/adversarial/conflict robustness central to robust RAG taxonomy. Application of RAG with retrieval improvements rather than a study of RAG failure modes.
C03_notes: KGI system extends DPR with hard negative mining (mitigates retrieval noise/hard negatives in training) and evaluates domain adaptation (zero/few-shot TACRED). 'Robust' refers to training robustness and domain transfer rather than adversarial/conflicting evidence handling. Boundary support for robust RAG.

title: SeRTS: Self-Rewarding Tree Search for Biomedical Retrieval-Augmented Generation
C02_notes: Biomedical RAG method using MCTS and self-rewarding tree search to improve retrieval quality. Focuses on performance enhancement, not robustness analysis, noise/distraction/conflict, adversarial defense, or calibration. Out of scope for robust RAG map.
C03_notes: SeRTS proposes a self-rewarding MCTS-based retrieval method for biomedical RAG to find more relevant documents and PPO-train LLMs. It is a general RAG retrieval improvement in a domain setting; it does not explicitly study unreliable evidence, adversarial corruption, knowledge conflict, calibration/abstention, or robustness evaluation. Closest taxonomy bucket is noisy_retrieval (improving retrieval quality), but contribution is not centrally about robustness, so out of scope.

title: Self-Retrieval: End-to-End Information Retrieval with One Large Language Model
C02_notes: Paper proposes Self-Retrieval, an end-to-end generative IR architecture using one LLM for indexing, retrieval, and reranking. While RAG is mentioned as a downstream beneficiary, the paper does not study robustness aspects (noise, distraction, conflict, attacks, uncertainty, calibration). It is generic retrieval methodology, out of scope for the robust RAG map.
C03_notes: Proposes Self-Retrieval, a unified end-to-end IR architecture inside a single LLM (indexing/retrieval/reranking via constrained decoding and self-assessment). Evaluated on NQ/TriviaQA/MS MARCO and downstream RAG quality. No contribution on unreliable-evidence robustness, adversarial corruption, noisy/conflicting context handling, calibration, or answerability. Out of scope for robust RAG map.

title: Superposition Prompting: Improving and Accelerating Retrieval-Augmented Generation
C02_notes: ICML 2024 paper targeting the distraction phenomenon in RAG where irrelevant context degrades output. Proposes superposition prompting with path pruning to discard irrelevant documents, improving robustness and efficiency on QA benchmarks.
C03_notes: ICML 2024 paper proposing superposition prompting for RAG. Explicitly addresses the 'distraction phenomenon' where irrelevant retrieved context degrades quality, using path pruning to discard irrelevant documents based on importance metric. Although the main framing is efficiency/acceleration, the path pruning mechanism is a concrete mitigation for distraction in long-context RAG, which makes it relevant to robust RAG. Evaluated on QA benchmarks (NaturalQuestions-Open) with accuracy + speed metrics.

title: TRACE: Grounding Time Series in Context for Multimodal Embedding and Retrieval
C02_notes: TRACE is a cross-modal time-series/text retriever for time-series foundation models with RAG. Focus is on building a domain-specific multimodal retriever and embeddings for forecasting/classification, not on robustness analysis. No study of noise, distractors, conflicts, adversarial attacks, calibration, or answerability. Out of scope for robust RAG map.
C03_notes: TRACE is a cross-modal time-series/text retriever for RAG augmentation of time-series foundation models. Its contributions are channel-level alignment and hard negative mining for retrieval quality, plus state-of-the-art encoder performance. It does not study unreliable evidence, noisy/distracting/conflicting/adversarial retrieval, calibration, or answerability for robust RAG. Closest taxonomy is multimodal_agentic_code (multimodal RAG setting), but no specific robustness mechanism — out of scope.

title: Towards Cross-Cultural Machine Translation with Retrieval-Augmented Generation from Multilingual Knowledge Graphs
C02_notes: Domain-specific RAG application for cross-cultural machine translation using multilingual knowledge graphs. Introduces XC-Translate benchmark and KG-MT method, but focus is on translation quality of cultural entity names, not RAG robustness. No analysis of retrieval noise, distraction, conflicts, or attacks.
C03_notes: Domain-specific RAG application: integrates multilingual KG retrieval into NMT for cross-cultural entity translation. Introduces XC-Translate benchmark and KG-MT method, but evaluation is about translation quality (BLEU/COMET/M-ETA), not about unreliable evidence, robustness, adversarial corruption, conflict, calibration, or answerability. No contribution to robust RAG under unreliable evidence.

title: Two-tiered Encoder-based Hallucination Detection for Retrieval-Augmented Generation in the Wild
C02_notes: Proposes RAGHalu, a two-tiered encoder-based hallucination/faithfulness detector for enterprise RAG. Directly addresses ungrounded responses (knowledge conflict between LLM output and KB) and supports abstain/escalation control; introduces re-annotated datasets. Relevant as supporting evidence for robust RAG faithfulness detection.
C03_notes: Proposes RAGHalu, a two-tiered encoder-based hallucination detector for enterprise RAG that classifies LLM response sentences as VERIFIABLE/NO-INFO then SUPPORTED/UNSUPPORTED against retrieved KB articles. Addresses contextual faithfulness (response vs. evidence) and serves as a guardrail for human-in-the-loop escalation. Also releases re-annotated public dataset. Fits knowledge_conflict (contextual faithfulness) with secondary control and benchmark aspects. EMNLP Industry Track.

title: Unified Generative and Discriminative Training for Multi-modal Large Language Models
C02_notes: Paper focuses on unifying generative and discriminative training paradigms for multimodal LLMs. While it mentions using RAG as a downstream strategy to enhance generative task performance, the primary contribution is on training methodology (Dynamic Time Warping, structure-induced constraints), not on robustness, evaluation, attacks, defenses, or calibration of RAG systems. No specific robust RAG angle.
C03_notes: Paper proposes a unified generative+discriminative training strategy (Sugar) for MLLMs to improve fine-grained semantic and retrieval performance. RAG is only mentioned as a downstream application enabled by the unified model. No contribution on unreliable evidence, retrieval noise, conflict, adversarial robustness, calibration, or evaluation of robust RAG. Out of scope.

title: WebBrain: Learning to Generate Factually Correct Articles for Queries by Grounding on Large Web Corpus
C02_notes: WebBrain introduces a dataset and ReGen framework for generating factual Wikipedia-style articles grounded on web evidence. While related to retrieval-augmented generation and factuality, it focuses on a new generation task rather than robustness analysis (no explicit study of noisy/adversarial retrieval, conflicts, calibration, or robustness perturbations). Background only.
C03_notes: Introduces WebBrain task/dataset and ReGen framework for generating factual Wikipedia-style articles grounded on web corpus. Focus is on hallucination reduction via better retrieval+citation+pretraining, not on specific unreliable-evidence robustness (noise analysis, conflict, attacks, calibration). Treated as background grounded-generation benchmark rather than core robust RAG contribution.

title: Chain of Agents: Large Language Models Collaborating on Long-Context Tasks
C02_notes: Proposes Chain-of-Agents multi-agent framework for long-context tasks. RAG appears only as a comparison baseline; the paper is about long-context processing alternatives, not about robust RAG mechanisms, retrieval noise, or RAG evaluation. Touches lost-in-the-middle issue but not as a robust RAG contribution. Out of scope.
C03_notes: Proposes Chain-of-Agents multi-agent framework for long-context tasks (QA, summarization, code completion); uses RAG only as a baseline. Touches on 'lost in the middle' long-context focus issue but does not address unreliable evidence, retrieval noise, adversarial corruption, conflict, calibration, or robustness evaluation. General capability/efficiency method for long-context, not robust RAG.

title: ChatQA 2: Bridging the Gap to Proprietary LLMs in Long Context and RAG Capabilities
C02_notes: ChatQA 2 builds a long-context plus RAG capable open model and evaluates on ChatRAGBench. Touches RAG robustness via chunk-size variation and top-k retrieval trade-offs (irrelevant context with large k), and explicitly compares long-context vs RAG. Primarily a capability/evaluation paper rather than a robustness-focused study, so support-level.
C03_notes: Primarily a capability-building paper for long-context LLM + RAG (extending Llama3 to 128K, training recipe, RAG vs long-context comparison). Mentions robustness to chunk size and analyzes top-k tradeoffs (fragmentation/irrelevance), but these are secondary findings, not focused on unreliable evidence, conflicts, adversarial inputs, calibration, or answerability. Closest taxonomy fit is noisy_retrieval, but contribution is general RAG/long-context performance.

title: ChatQA: Surpassing GPT-4 on Conversational QA and RAG
C02_notes: ChatQA introduces ChatRAG Bench including unanswerable scenarios and conversational RAG evaluation; relevant to RAG benchmarking and answerability/abstention, though primary contribution is instruction tuning recipe for RAG/conversational QA.
C03_notes: ChatQA's primary contribution is a two-stage instruction tuning recipe to build a strong open conversational QA/RAG model competitive with GPT-4, plus ChatRAG Bench (10 datasets). It briefly addresses unanswerable questions/hallucination avoidance, but this is one of four contributions and not a focused robustness study under unreliable evidence. Treated as background general-RAG capability paper; unanswerable handling gives weak support relevance only.

title: Deliberation on Priors: Trustworthy Reasoning of Large Language Models on Knowledge Graphs
C02_notes: KG-RAG method using priors and introspection for faithful reasoning; not focused on robustness to noise, conflicts, or attacks.
C03_notes: KG-RAG method (DP) that improves KGQA accuracy via knowledge distillation of structural priors and a reasoning-introspection module that verifies extracted constraints and triggers backtracking. The 'trustworthy' framing is about faithful KG reasoning paths, not handling unreliable/noisy evidence, conflicting sources, adversarial corruption, or answerability. Closest taxonomy label is calibration_control due to introspection/verification with backtracking, but core contribution is a KGQA accuracy method rather than a robust-RAG-under-unreliable-evidence contribution; out of scope.

title: Do Metadata and Appearance of the Retrieved Webpages Affect LLM's Reasoning in Retrieval-Augmented Generation?
C02_notes: Studies how non-textual metadata (publication time, source, visual appearance) of retrieved webpages affects LLM reasoning when documents present conflicting evidence in RAG. Directly addresses knowledge conflict and source preference in RAG; also introduces ConflictingQA-Fake dataset. BlackboxNLP workshop venue, useful supporting evidence for robust RAG map.
C03_notes: Studies how non-textual metadata (publication time, source credibility, webpage appearance) affects LLM reasoning when retrieved documents present conflicting evidence. Uses ConflictingQA and introduces ConflictingQA-FAKE. Core knowledge_conflict analysis with implications for adversarial manipulation (acknowledged in ethics). BlackboxNLP workshop at EMNLP 2024.

title: Optimizing LLM Based Retrieval Augmented Generation Pipelines in the Financial Domain
C02_notes: Empirical study benchmarks 6 LLMs across 15 retrieval conditions and 9 prompts on two financial RAG datasets. Probes robustness to missing gold docs, distractor count, and document ordering, plus prompt sensitivity. Relevant as evaluation/analysis evidence for retrieval-noise and distraction robustness in RAG.
C03_notes: NAACL Industry Track financial-domain RAG benchmark. Systematically varies retrieval quality (gold doc presence, number of retrieved docs, ordering) across 6 LLMs and 9 prompts to study impact on answer generation. Explicitly analyzes distractor documents and missing gold doc effects, plus pseudo-helpfulness/hallucination when evidence is missing. Fits noisy_retrieval (retrieval imperfection analysis) with distraction and evaluation_benchmark as secondary. Not a method contribution but useful empirical support.

title: Position: Retrieval-augmented systems can be dangerous medical communicators
C02_notes: ICML position paper analyzing pragmatic misalignment in medical RAG; decontextualization and selective context cause misleading outputs despite literal accuracy
C03_notes: ICML position paper arguing that RAG systems in medicine are 'pragmatically misaligned': even when individual facts are accurate, selective extraction and failure to reason about implicit query presuppositions/biases (e.g., 'why is X dangerous' vs. 'why is X safe', symptoms of disputed conditions) yield misleading outputs. Large-scale query study with LLM-as-judge evaluation. Primary failure framed as ambiguous/underspecified queries with implicit presuppositions (ood_uncertainty); also relates to selective context use (distraction) in a domain-specific (medical) RAG setting. Useful supporting/positioning work rather than a core method or benchmark resource.

title: Reasoning-Enhanced Healthcare Predictions with Knowledge Graph Community Retrieval
C02_notes: Domain-specific KG-enhanced RAG for healthcare prediction (mortality/readmission on MIMIC). Focuses on improving prediction accuracy via KG community retrieval, not on robustness, noise analysis, adversarial attacks, conflicts, calibration, or RAG evaluation/benchmarking. Out of scope for robust RAG map.
C03_notes: KARE is a domain-specific healthcare RAG framework that uses KG community retrieval plus LLM reasoning for mortality/readmission prediction on MIMIC-III/IV. It motivates the work by noting traditional RAG retrieves 'sparse or irrelevant' info, but the core contribution is a new KG-construction + retrieval + fine-tuning pipeline for accuracy on clinical prediction, not an analysis/mitigation of unreliable evidence, conflict, attack, or calibration. Boundary multimodal/domain-specific RAG application; not core to robust-RAG map.

title: Reducing hallucination in structured outputs via Retrieval-Augmented Generation
C02_notes: Industry application paper using RAG to reduce hallucination in JSON workflow generation. Mentions OOD generalization and hallucination reduction, but it is primarily an applied system description, not a robustness study/benchmark/attack-defense. No analysis of retrieval noise, conflicts, distractors, or calibration mechanisms specific to robust RAG. Boundary/background only.
C03_notes: Industry application paper deploying RAG to reduce hallucination in structured JSON workflow generation. Trains a domain-specific retriever and fine-tunes LLM with retrieved context; main contributions are practical (reduced hallucination, smaller LLM footprint, OOD generalization) rather than a robustness/unreliable-evidence analysis. No study of adversarial inputs, knowledge conflicts, calibration, or noisy/distracting retrieval as an explicit research axis. Closest taxonomy fit is noisy_retrieval because of retriever-LLM alignment for entity grounding, but the paper does not analyze retrieval noise per se.

title: SV-RAG: LoRA-Contextualizing Adaptation of  MLLMs for Long Document Understanding
C02_notes: SV-RAG is a multimodal RAG framework using LoRA-adapted MLLMs for long visually-rich document understanding. Focus is on efficiency and accuracy, not robustness, noise, conflict, or adversarial issues. Out of scope for robust RAG map.
C03_notes: SV-RAG is a multimodal RAG framework using LoRA-adapted MLLMs for long visually-rich document understanding. Focus is on efficient evidence page retrieval and QA, not on unreliable evidence, robustness, adversarial attacks, conflict, calibration, or answerability. VisR-Bench is a standard QA benchmark without robustness/perturbation axes. Out of scope for robust RAG map.

title: SearchLVLMs: A Plug-and-Play Framework for Augmenting Large Vision-Language Models by Searching Up-to-Date Internet Knowledge
C02_notes: Multimodal internet-augmented generation framework with hierarchical filtering and UDK-VQA benchmark; addresses up-to-date knowledge for LVLMs but not explicitly a robustness study.
C03_notes: Plug-and-play internet-augmented generation framework for LVLMs to access up-to-date knowledge via search engines. Includes hierarchical website/content filtering and a new UDK-VQA benchmark. The filtering touches on noisy web retrieval, but the paper's primary contribution is enabling multimodal IAG for fresh knowledge rather than analyzing/mitigating unreliable evidence, conflicts, or adversarial corruption. Boundary multimodal RAG application.

title: Vgent: Graph-based Retrieval-Reasoning-Augmented Generation For Long Video Understanding
C02_notes: Vgent proposes a graph-based RAG framework for long video understanding. While it touches on retrieval noise and distraction from irrelevant clips, the focus is on improving video QA accuracy via graph structure and structured reasoning, not on systematic robustness analysis, attack/defense, or calibration in RAG. Best treated as adjacent multimodal RAG background, not core robust RAG evidence.
C03_notes: Graph-based RAG for long video understanding. Explicitly addresses retrieval noise and distraction by hard-negative retrieved clips via a structured post-retrieval reasoning/verification step. Robustness mechanism is tailored to the video/multimodal setting (graph over clips + structured query decomposition), so multimodal_agentic_code is primary with noisy_retrieval and distraction as secondary. Evaluation is mainly QA accuracy on MLVU/VideoMME/LongVideoBench, not a robustness benchmark per se, hence support rather than core.

title: VimoRAG: Video-based Retrieval-augmented 3D Motion Generation for Motion Language Models
C02_notes: Domain-specific video-based RAG for 3D motion generation. While it addresses error propagation from noisy retrieval, it is not about robust RAG for LLM text/QA systems and falls outside the map scope.
C03_notes: Domain-specific (3D motion generation) cross-modal video-based RAG. Explicitly identifies and addresses error propagation from inaccurate/low-quality retrieved videos via McDPO, which teaches the LLM when to use/ignore noisy retrieved video signals. Robustness contribution is real but secondary to introducing the new motion-RAG paradigm; primary label set to multimodal_agentic_code with noisy_retrieval as secondary. Boundary support evidence for robust RAG under unreliable evidence.

title: Visual Haystacks: A Vision-Centric Needle-In-A-Haystack Benchmark
C02_notes: Introduces Visual Haystacks benchmark for multi-image RAG, evaluates visual distractors and positional bias (lost-in-the-middle), and proposes MIRAGE visual-RAG framework. Relevant as multimodal robust RAG benchmark.
C03_notes: Vision-centric NIAH benchmark for multi-image QA; explicitly evaluates visual distractor susceptibility, multi-image reasoning failures, and positional ('lost-in-the-middle') bias in long-context LMMs. Also introduces MIRAGE visual-RAG framework as mitigation. Primary contribution is benchmark; distraction and multimodal RAG robustness are key axes.

title: A Theory for Token-Level Harmonization in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
C02_notes: ICLR 2025 paper provides theoretical framework for token-level trade-off between benefit and detriment in RAG, addressing noisy retrieval and knowledge conflict via Tok-RAG collaborative generation between pure LLM and RAG.
C03_notes: ICLR 2025 paper provides theoretical framework decomposing RAG token prediction into benefit (distribution completion) and detriment (distribution contradiction from noisy/incorrect retrieval). Proposes Tok-RAG, a token-level collaborative generation method that decides whether to trust RAG output or pure LLM at each token without training/evaluators. Primary contribution is a control/calibration mechanism for trusting evidence; addresses knowledge conflict between parametric and retrieved knowledge and noisy retrieval as underlying failure modes.

title: Active Retrieval Augmented Generation
C02_notes: FLARE proposes active retrieval that decides when (low-probability tokens trigger retrieval) and what to retrieve (anticipated next sentence as query) during long-form generation. This is a canonical adaptive/calibrated retrieval control method, directly relevant to robust RAG. Evaluated on multihop QA, commonsense reasoning, long-form QA, and open-domain summarization. EMNLP 2023 main conference.
C03_notes: FLARE proposes active/adaptive retrieval that triggers re-retrieval when LM emits low-confidence tokens during generation, and uses forward-looking next-sentence as query. This is a calibration-based control mechanism for when/what to retrieve (well-calibrated LM probabilities used as a trigger). Also notes that low-confidence tokens can distract retrievers (secondary: distraction). Evaluated on long-form QA and summarization.

title: An Information Bottleneck Perspective for Effective Noise Filtering on Retrieval-Augmented Generation
C02_notes: ACL 2024 long paper introducing an information bottleneck-based noise filter for RAG. Directly targets noisy/irrelevant retrieved passages, proposes SFT and RL training objectives, and evaluates on NQ, TriviaQA, HotpotQA. Core robust RAG contribution addressing noisy retrieval and context distraction via context-assembly filtering.
C03_notes: ACL 2024 long paper. Introduces Information Bottleneck principle to train a noise filter for RAG that compresses retrieved passages, explicitly removing irrelevant/noisy content while preserving info needed for the answer. Handles case where retrieval is irrelevant by compressing to empty. Directly targets unreliable-evidence (noisy retrieval) with defense/mitigation via context-assembly filtering. Evaluated on NQ/TriviaQA/HotpotQA for correctness and compression rate.

title: Auto-GDA: Automatic Domain Adaptation for Efficient Grounding Verification in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
C02_notes: ICLR 2025 paper on Auto-GDA, domain adaptation framework for lightweight NLI-based grounding verification in RAG. Addresses faithfulness verification of LLM output against retrieved evidence, directly relevant to robust RAG hallucination detection and control.
C03_notes: ICLR 2025 paper proposing Auto-GDA, an unsupervised synthetic-data domain adaptation framework to train lightweight NLI models for grounding verification (faithfulness checking) of RAG outputs. Directly addresses hallucination/ungrounded generation by enabling efficient post-hoc verification that the answer is supported by retrieved evidence. Primary label is knowledge_conflict (contextual faithfulness); calibration_control is secondary because the verifier supports trust/abstain decisions.

title: BEIR: A Heterogeneous Benchmark for Zero-shot Evaluation of Information Retrieval Models
C02_notes: BEIR is a heterogeneous zero-shot IR benchmark explicitly targeting OOD generalization across 18 datasets and 9 tasks. Widely used as a retrieval robustness/OOD evaluation resource underpinning RAG retriever evaluation.
C03_notes: BEIR is a heterogeneous zero-shot IR benchmark covering 18 datasets across 9 tasks to evaluate OOD generalization of retrievers (lexical, sparse, dense, late-interaction, re-ranking). It is foundational infrastructure for retrieval evaluation but does not study RAG under unreliable evidence (no generator robustness, no conflict/adversarial/distractor analysis at the RAG level). Useful background for retrieval-quality framing but not a core robust-RAG contribution.

title: Benchmarking Multimodal Retrieval Augmented Generation with Dynamic VQA Dataset and Self-adaptive Planning Agent
C02_notes: Introduces Dyn-VQA benchmark for multimodal RAG with dynamic, multi-hop and time-varying questions, plus a self-adaptive planning agent (OmniSearch). Relevant as multimodal RAG benchmark and adaptive retrieval control.
C03_notes: ICLR 2025 paper proposes Dyn-VQA benchmark (rapidly-changing answers, multimodal, multi-hop questions) and OmniSearch self-adaptive planning agent for multimodal RAG. Addresses rigidity of heuristic mRAG: outdated vs. newer mixed knowledge and overloaded queries. Robustness contribution is in the multimodal agentic setting via adaptive retrieval planning; also serves as benchmark. Primary label set to multimodal_agentic_code since the mechanism is unique to multimodal agentic RAG.

title: Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine
C02_notes: MIRAGE benchmark systematically evaluates RAG components (corpora, retrievers, LLMs) for medical QA, including analysis of lost-in-the-middle effects and scaling. Provides domain-specific RAG evaluation resource relevant to robust RAG.
C03_notes: MIRAGE benchmark + MedRAG toolkit for systematic evaluation of medical RAG across 5 corpora, 4 retrievers, 6 LLMs on 5 medical QA datasets. Primary contribution is finding optimal RAG configurations for medicine. Touches on context-utilization (lost-in-the-middle effect, log-linear scaling) as secondary analysis, but lacks explicit focus on unreliable evidence, adversarial robustness, knowledge conflict, or selective answerability. Domain-specific benchmark; boundary context for robust-RAG map.

title: Boosting Knowledge Utilization in Multimodal Large Language Models via Adaptive Logits Fusion and Attention Reallocation
C02_notes: ALFAR explicitly tackles knowledge conflicts between parametric and contextual knowledge in MRAG, plus attention bias (distraction-like) on retrieved context. Training-free generator-side intervention (logits fusion + attention reallocation) directly relevant to robust RAG. Multimodal setting is secondary.
C03_notes: ALFAR explicitly targets two robust-RAG issues in MRAG: (1) knowledge conflicts between parametric and retrieved contextual knowledge, and (2) attention bias diluting relevant context tokens. Training-free, plug-and-play generator-side method using adaptive logits fusion and attention reallocation. Shows robustness across varying contextual-knowledge quality (including noisy retrievals). Multimodal-specific but addresses core unreliable-evidence concerns.

title: Chain-of-Retrieval Augmented Generation
C02_notes: CoRAG trains LLMs to iteratively retrieve and reformulate queries to handle imperfect retrieval, with claimed robustness against retrievers of varying quality. Adaptive retrieval control relevant to robust RAG.
C03_notes: CoRAG trains LLMs to iteratively retrieve and reformulate queries, dynamically deciding next retrieval action based on state. Addresses imperfect single-step retrieval and reports robustness across retrievers of varying quality. Primary contribution is adaptive/iterative retrieval (calibration_control); secondary touches noisy retrieval mitigation. Not focused on adversarial or unanswerable settings, hence support-level.

title: ColPali: Efficient Document Retrieval with Vision Language Models
C02_notes: ColPali introduces a vision-language document retrieval model and ViDoRe benchmark. It motivates RAG pipelines but does not address robustness, noise, adversarial attacks, conflicts, or calibration. Background only for visual RAG retrieval.
C03_notes: ColPali introduces a vision-language document retrieval method and the ViDoRe benchmark for visually rich document retrieval. The contribution is about retrieval efficiency/quality on visual documents for downstream RAG, not about unreliable evidence, robustness, conflict, adversarial corruption, calibration, or answerability. Benchmark evaluates standard retrieval utility, no perturbation/threat axis. Closest taxonomy label is multimodal_agentic_code (multimodal RAG setting) but no robustness mechanism specific to the setting; out of scope for robust RAG map.

title: DRAGIN: Dynamic Retrieval Augmented Generation based on the Real-time Information Needs of Large Language Models
